steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: Our primary objective as penholder is to secure a clean, unified 12-month renewal of UNSMIL’s mandate to maintain operational continuity and provide sustained diplomatic backing for UN mediation efforts towards national elections. Key negotiating sensitivities are expected around references to the independence of sovereign institutions following recent tensions at the Libyan Audit Bureau and Central Bank, calls for the withdrawal of foreign fighters and mercenaries, and language regarding civil society and human rights protections, where Russia and China may resist detailed operational guidance.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) and all its subsequent resolutions on Libya, including resolutions 2259 (2015), 2510 (2020), 2542 (2020), 2570 (2021), 2629 (2022), 2656 (2022), 2702 (2023), 2755 (2024), 2769 (2025), 2796 (2025), and 2819 (2026), and its relevant Presidential Statements,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and the need to refrain from external interference,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, which will enable the holding of free, fair, transparent and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections across Libya as soon as possible, in order to end the transitional period and unify state institutions,

Urging all Libyan stakeholders to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise with the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) to resolve all outstanding politically contentious issues, and calling upon all political actors to refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions, undermine trust, and destabilise the political and security environment,

Welcoming the efforts of UNSMIL and the ongoing dialogue among Libyan institutions, including consultations on sovereign positions, and encouraging continued constructive engagement to achieve broad consensus on the constitutional and legal frameworks necessary for credible national elections,

Emphasising the vital importance of the independence, integrity, and unified functioning of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau, condemning any attempts to use force, intimidation, or unilateral measures against these institutions or their personnel, and reiterating that Libya’s natural resources belong to all Libyans and must be managed in a transparent, equitable, and accountable manner,

Welcoming progress made towards financial arrangements and the implementation of a unified national budget, as noted in resolution 2819 (2026), and urging relevant Libyan authorities to maintain fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability for the benefit of the entire Libyan population,

Reiterating its grave concern at the fragile security environment, clashes between armed groups, and the continued proliferation of arms and ammunition, stressing the urgent need for comprehensive security sector reform and the disarmament, demobilisation, and reintegration (DDR) of armed groups and non-state actors, and calling for the full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the withdrawal without further delay of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries,

Commending the ongoing work of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and Libyan security authorities towards the reunification of military and security institutions, and welcoming efforts to clear explosive remnants of war and unexploded ordnance across affected regions,

Reaffirming that all parties must comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law, as applicable, expressing concern over the human rights situation in Libya, including reports of arbitrary detention, restrictions on civic space, and abuses against migrants and refugees, and underscoring the necessity of creating an enabling environment for civil society organisations, human rights defenders, and media professionals to operate safely and independently,

Underlining the importance of the full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation of women, as well as the active engagement of youth, in all stages of the political process, peacebuilding, and national reconciliation efforts,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) until 31 October 2027, as an integrated special political mission, in accordance with resolution 2629 (2022) and subsequent resolutions;

2. Calls upon all Libyan stakeholders and key regional and international actors to support UNSMIL’s mandate and the United Nations-facilitated political process, and to engage constructively with the Mission to advance a sustainable political settlement and the holding of national elections;

3. Reaffirms UNSMIL’s role in supporting Libyan-led efforts towards national reconciliation, security sector reform, human rights monitoring, and the transparent and equitable management of public revenues and economic governance;

4. Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council on the implementation of this resolution every 60 days;

5. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

messages.Bahrain: Bahrain commends the United Kingdom for presenting a balanced draft that extends UNSMIL's mandate for a full year, providing vital stability for the mission's good offices. We reiterate our steadfast support for Libya's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, fighters, and mercenaries without delay. Emphasizing the constructive role of regional partners, particularly the League of Arab States, will further strengthen collective efforts to support an inclusive Libyan-led political settlement.
messages.China: China supports the one-year extension of UNSMIL's mandate and appreciates the United Kingdom's efforts as penholder to advance a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We believe the draft should adequately reflect recent Council consensus, particularly from resolutions 2769 (2025) and 2819 (2026), regarding the preservation of the value of Libya's frozen assets and combating illicit oil smuggling. We hope the penholder will incorporate these constructive proposals to maintain Council unity.
messages.Colombia: Colombia fully supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate for twelve months and commends the United Kingdom for a well-balanced text. To ensure sustainable peace, we encourage strengthening language on the protection of the human rights of migrants and refugees, as well as recognizing transitional justice and accountability alongside national reconciliation efforts. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to adopt this resolution smoothly.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo commends the United Kingdom for circulating a balanced draft renewing UNSMIL's mandate for a full year. As an African member of the Council, we attach high importance to acknowledging the vital partnership with the African Union and neighbouring states, especially regarding the national reconciliation track and regional security. We look forward to seeing these constructive additions reflected in the next revision.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the UK's draft renewing UNSMIL's mandate for a full twelve months and commends the text's balanced approach. To ensure the resolution adequately addresses key drivers of instability and impunity, we propose reinforcing the call for strict compliance with the UN arms embargo and emphasizing accountability for human rights violations and abuses. We look forward to working closely with the penholder and Council colleagues towards a swift, unanimous adoption.
messages.France: France strongly supports the UK's draft renewing UNSMIL's mandate for a full year and commends the balanced reflection of recent political and financial developments. To further reinforce the security track, we believe it is vital to explicitly recall Member States' obligations under the arms embargo and to explicitly reaffirm UNSMIL's support for the 5+5 JMC and ceasefire monitoring. We stand ready to work closely with the penholder to ensure a swift, unanimous adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft circulated by the United Kingdom and fully supports extending UNSMIL's mandate for twelve months to ensure vital political continuity. We request the inclusion of explicit language in PP8 calling on all Member States to strictly uphold and comply with the UN arms embargo. Full respect for the arms embargo and the complete withdrawal without delay of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries remain indispensable for the stability of Libya and the broader Mediterranean region.
messages.Latvia: Latvia commends the United Kingdom for presenting a well-balanced draft resolution providing UNSMIL with a stable 12-month mandate renewal. We strongly welcome the text's focus on advancing a credible Libyan-led political process towards elections, protecting the independence of sovereign economic institutions, and demanding the withdrawal of all foreign forces and mercenaries. Incorporating explicit reference to accountability for human rights violations and abuses would further strengthen the Council's support for the rule of law and sustainable peace in Libya.
messages.Liberia: Liberia welcomes the draft resolution renewing UNSMIL's mandate for twelve months and commends the United Kingdom for its balanced text. We strongly support the Mission's vital role in advancing a Libyan-owned and Libyan-led political process, while emphasizing the crucial contribution of regional partners, particularly the African Union, in facilitating inclusive national reconciliation. Liberia stands ready to work constructively with all delegations to ensure the prompt adoption of this resolution.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNSMIL for twelve months and appreciates the United Kingdom's balanced drafting as penholder. As a brotherly country to Libya, Pakistan reaffirms its steadfast commitment to Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity, through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We propose a modest addition in operative paragraph 3 to highlight institutional capacity-building, which is essential for enabling Libyan authorities to independently shoulder key state responsibilities and achieve sustainable stability.
messages.Panama: Panama commends the United Kingdom for presenting a balanced draft resolution and fully supports the twelve-month extension of UNSMIL's mandate. In line with our established position, we request the re-insertion of agreed language emphasizing the preservation and protection of Libya's frozen assets so that they remain safeguarded for the ultimate benefit of the Libyan people. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and all Council colleagues towards the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate for another twelve-month period and appreciates the penholder's efforts to maintain Council unity on Libya. However, the draft must retain agreed language regarding the withdrawal of foreign forces and mercenaries, which must proceed in a synchronized, phased, gradual, and balanced manner in line with the 5+5 JMC Action Plan so as not to destabilize the delicate security balance. Additionally, the text should clearly underscore the necessity for UNSMIL to expand its geographical presence across the entire country, including Benghazi and Sabha, to ensure impartial and balanced mediation.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of UNSMIL's mandate for twelve months and appreciates the United Kingdom's stewardship as penholder. In line with the long-standing priorities of the A3, we request the inclusion of language reaffirming the need to safeguard Libya's frozen assets from erosion and misuse for the benefit of the Libyan people, building on resolution 2819 (2026). We also underscore the necessity of recognizing the essential role of neighbouring countries and regional organizations, particularly the African Union, in supporting national reconciliation and sustaining peace.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks the United Kingdom for circulating a strong and timely draft extending UNSMIL's mandate for a full year. We strongly welcome the draft's firm condemnation of attacks against sovereign institutions, notably the Audit Bureau and the Central Bank of Libya. We ask the penholder to incorporate our targeted additions reflecting resolution 2819 (2026) regarding the transparent routing of oil revenues and supporting the implementation of Libya's unified budget.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United Kingdom accommodated broad Council consensus by incorporating agreed language on the arms embargo, frozen assets, oil revenue transparency, human rights accountability, and regional cooperation with the African Union and the League of Arab States. Balanced language was also included regarding the withdrawal of foreign forces and the expansion of UNSMIL's presence throughout Libya, ensuring unanimous support across all permanent and elected members.

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) and all its subsequent resolutions on Libya, including resolutions 2259 (2015), 2510 (2020), 2542 (2020), 2570 (2021), 2629 (2022), 2656 (2022), 2702 (2023), 2755 (2024), 2769 (2025), 2796 (2025), and 2819 (2026), and its relevant Presidential Statements,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and the need to refrain from external interference,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, which will enable the holding of free, fair, transparent and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections across Libya as soon as possible, in order to end the transitional period and unify state institutions,

Urging all Libyan stakeholders to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise with the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) to resolve all outstanding politically contentious issues, and calling upon all political actors to refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions, undermine trust, and destabilise the political and security environment,

Reaffirming its intention to ensure that assets frozen pursuant to paragraph 17 of resolution 1970 (2011) shall at a later stage be made available to and for the benefit of the Libyan people, and calling upon relevant Member States to protect frozen assets for the future benefit of the Libyan people, including by preserving their value and preventing their misuse and misappropriation, in accordance with resolutions 2769 (2025) and 2819 (2026),

Reiterating its grave concern at the fragile security environment, clashes between armed groups, and the continued proliferation of arms and ammunition, calling upon all Member States to comply fully with the arms embargo established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011) and subsequent resolutions, stressing the urgent need for comprehensive security sector reform and the disarmament, demobilisation, and reintegration (DDR) of armed groups and non-state actors, and calling for the full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the withdrawal without further delay of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries, and the implementation of the Action Plan approved by the 5+5 Joint Military Commission in a synchronized, phased, gradual and balanced manner,

Underlining the importance of the full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation of women, as well as the active engagement of youth, in all stages of the political process, peacebuilding, and national reconciliation efforts,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) until 31 October 2027, as an integrated special political mission, in accordance with resolution 2629 (2022) and subsequent resolutions;

2. Calls upon all Libyan stakeholders and key regional and international actors, including the League of Arab States, the African Union, and neighbouring countries, to support UNSMIL’s mandate and the United Nations-facilitated political process, and to engage constructively with the Mission to advance a sustainable political settlement and the holding of national elections;

3. messages.Bahrain: The Kingdom of Bahrain expresses its sincere appreciation to the penholder for accommodating our proposal to highlight the vital role of the League of Arab States and neighbouring countries in OP2. The revised draft effectively balances the political, security, and economic priorities needed to advance stability and unity across Libya under a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned process. Bahrain is fully satisfied with the current text and looks forward to voting in favour of its adoption.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for accommodating our proposals regarding the preservation of frozen Libyan assets and combating illicit oil smuggling. The revised draft strikes a balanced approach that respects Libya's sovereignty and ownership while providing sound support to UNSMIL. China supports the adoption of the draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Colombia: Colombia expresses its appreciation to the United Kingdom as penholder for constructively incorporating our proposals regarding transitional justice, accountability, and the protection of the human rights of migrants and refugees. The current draft strikes an appropriate balance and provides UNSMIL with the necessary framework to support Libya's political and economic stability. Colombia fully supports the draft resolution and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo thanks the penholder for accommodating our proposals regarding the essential role of the African Union, its High-Level Committee on Libya, and regional partners. We welcome the balanced nature of the revised draft, which appropriately reinforces support for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process while ensuring UNSMIL's operational continuity. The DRC fully supports the adoption of the draft resolution as currently formulated.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our proposals regarding compliance with the arms embargo and accountability for human rights and international humanitarian law violations. We find the revised draft well-balanced, addressing key political, security, human rights, and economic priorities while granting UNSMIL the necessary mandate and stability to carry out its vital work. Denmark fully supports the draft resolution as presented and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.France: France welcomes revision 1 and thanks the United Kingdom for positively incorporating our proposals on the arms embargo and UNSMIL's support to the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and the Libyan Ceasefire Monitoring Mechanism. The draft is balanced and addresses the essential priorities: revitalizing the political process towards credible elections, preserving the integrity of sovereign institutions, and maintaining security arrangements. France fully supports the text and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United Kingdom for accommodating our request regarding full compliance with the arms embargo in the revised text. We strongly support the twelve-month renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to advance an inclusive, Libyan-led political process, uphold the ceasefire agreement, and ensure the complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries. Greece stands ready to vote in favour of the draft resolution as currently drafted.
messages.Latvia: Latvia thanks the United Kingdom for its leadership as penholder and for incorporating our proposal on accountability for human rights and international humanitarian law violations in the revised text. We fully support this balanced draft resolution and the twelve-month extension of UNSMIL's mandate, which provides vital stability to advance the Libyan-led political process and security arrangements. We look forward to voting in favour of this text.
messages.Liberia: Liberia commends the United Kingdom for its constructive stewardship of this draft resolution and thanks the penholder for fully incorporating our request highlighting close coordination with the African Union and regional partners in operative paragraph 3. We believe the current text presents a balanced, comprehensive framework that appropriately supports UNSMIL's critical work, advances national reconciliation, and safeguards Libyan sovereignty. Liberia fully supports the draft resolution as presented and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposal on institutional capacity-building into operative paragraph 3. The current text strikes a balanced approach that respects Libya's sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity while reinforcing a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution and is prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United Kingdom for its constructive leadership as penholder and for incorporating our language regarding the preservation and safeguarding of Libya's frozen assets for the future benefit of its people. We fully support the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate for twelve months and the balanced approach of the draft resolution in supporting a Libyan-led political process, institutional integrity, and human rights. Panama is prepared to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation thanks the penholder for incorporating our key priorities into Revision 1, particularly the call for UNSMIL to expand its presence across the country, including in Benghazi and Sabha, and the inclusion of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission's Action Plan. The revised draft offers a balanced approach that supports a genuinely Libyan-led, Libyan-owned political process while respecting the existing security arrangements on the ground. We are ready to support the draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Somalia: Somalia commends the United Kingdom for its collaborative approach as penholder and for incorporating our priorities into Revision 1, notably regarding the preservation and protection of Libya's frozen assets and the recognition of the African Union and neighbouring countries. The draft strikes a well-calibrated balance that fully supports Libyan ownership, national reconciliation, and institutional unity. We are prepared to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, notably regarding the routing of oil revenues through the National Oil Corporation's accounts at the Libyan Foreign Bank and UNSMIL's support for the unified national budget. The text presents a strong, balanced framework that protects Libya's economic institutions, upholds the arms embargo, and empowers UNSMIL to advance an inclusive Libyan-led political process toward national elections. The United States fully supports the draft resolution as currently formulated and looks forward to voting in favour.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United Kingdom expresses its appreciation to all Council members for their constructive engagement and unanimous support for Revision 1. With all fifteen members expressing full satisfaction with the balanced text renewing UNSMIL's mandate until 31 October 2027, the draft resolution is retained without changes and submitted for adoption with anticipated unanimous support.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) and all its subsequent resolutions on Libya, including resolutions 2259 (2015), 2510 (2020), 2542 (2020), 2570 (2021), 2629 (2022), 2656 (2022), 2702 (2023), 2755 (2024), 2769 (2025), 2796 (2025), and 2819 (2026), and its relevant Presidential Statements,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and the need to refrain from external interference,

Reaffirming its strong commitment to an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, which will enable the holding of free, fair, transparent and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections across Libya as soon as possible, in order to end the transitional period and unify state institutions,

Urging all Libyan stakeholders to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise with the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) to resolve all outstanding politically contentious issues, and calling upon all political actors to refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions, undermine trust, and destabilise the political and security environment,

Welcoming the efforts of UNSMIL and the ongoing dialogue among Libyan institutions, including consultations on sovereign positions, and encouraging continued constructive engagement to achieve broad consensus on the constitutional and legal frameworks necessary for credible national elections,

Emphasising the vital importance of the independence, integrity, and unified functioning of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau, condemning any attempts to use force, intimidation, or unilateral measures against these institutions or their personnel, reiterating that Libya’s natural resources belong to all Libyans and must be managed in a transparent, equitable, and accountable manner, reiterating in this regard the call in resolution 2819 (2026) for payments for crude oil exports to be routed exclusively through the accounts of the National Oil Corporation at the Libyan Foreign Bank to prevent diversion of energy revenues, and stressing the need to strengthen efforts to combat the illicit export and smuggling of crude oil and refined petroleum products, ensuring that all related activities are conducted strictly under the auspices of the National Oil Corporation,

Welcoming progress made towards financial arrangements and the implementation of a unified national budget, as noted in resolution 2819 (2026), and urging relevant Libyan authorities to maintain fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability for the benefit of the entire Libyan population,

Reaffirming its intention to ensure that assets frozen pursuant to paragraph 17 of resolution 1970 (2011) shall at a later stage be made available to and for the benefit of the Libyan people, and calling upon relevant Member States to protect frozen assets for the future benefit of the Libyan people, including by preserving their value and preventing their misuse and misappropriation, in accordance with resolutions 2769 (2025) and 2819 (2026),

Reiterating its grave concern at the fragile security environment, clashes between armed groups, and the continued proliferation of arms and ammunition, calling upon all Member States to comply fully with the arms embargo established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011) and subsequent resolutions, stressing the urgent need for comprehensive security sector reform and the disarmament, demobilisation, and reintegration (DDR) of armed groups and non-state actors, and calling for the full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the withdrawal without further delay of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries, and the implementation of the Action Plan approved by the 5+5 Joint Military Commission in a synchronized, phased, gradual and balanced manner,

Commending the ongoing work of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and Libyan security authorities towards the reunification of military and security institutions, and welcoming efforts to clear explosive remnants of war and unexploded ordnance across affected regions,

Recognising the important role of neighbouring countries and regional organisations, in particular the African Union, its High-Level Committee on Libya, and the League of Arab States, in support of the United Nations and Libyan-led efforts towards sustainable peace and national reconciliation,

Reaffirming that all parties must comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law, as applicable, expressing concern over the human rights situation in Libya, including reports of arbitrary detention, restrictions on civic space, and abuses against migrants and refugees, calling upon the Libyan authorities to ensure the full protection of the human rights of all migrants and refugees, end arbitrary detention, and hold perpetrators of violations accountable, underscoring the critical importance of ensuring accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and violations and abuses of human rights, and underscoring the necessity of creating an enabling environment for civil society organisations, human rights defenders, and media professionals to operate safely and independently,

Underlining the importance of the full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation of women, as well as the active engagement of youth, in all stages of the political process, peacebuilding, and national reconciliation efforts,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) until 31 October 2027, as an integrated special political mission, in accordance with resolution 2629 (2022) and subsequent resolutions;

2. Calls upon all Libyan stakeholders and key regional and international actors, including the League of Arab States, the African Union, and neighbouring countries, to support UNSMIL’s mandate and the United Nations-facilitated political process, and to engage constructively with the Mission to advance a sustainable political settlement and the holding of national elections;

3. Reaffirms UNSMIL’s role in supporting Libyan-led efforts towards national reconciliation, transitional justice and accountability, in close coordination with the African Union and regional partners, security sector reform, support to the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and the Libyan Ceasefire Monitoring Mechanism, institutional capacity-building, human rights monitoring, and the transparent and equitable management of public revenues and economic governance, including support for the full and transparent implementation of Libya's unified national budget, and calls upon UNSMIL to continue expanding its presence throughout the country, including in Benghazi and Sabha, to ensure balanced and effective engagement with all Libyan stakeholders;

4. Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council on the implementation of this resolution every 60 days;

5. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

reasons.Bahrain: Bahrain fully supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate and an inclusive, Libyan-led political process leading to elections, consistent with its prior vote on resolution 2819 and its position during negotiations.
reasons.China: China supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to facilitate an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, and in line with its consistent practice and position in negotiations, China votes in favour without delivering a statement before the vote.
reasons.Colombia: Colombia fully supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to advance an inclusive, Libyan-led political process, promote national reconciliation, and protect human rights, in line with its consistent voting record on the agenda item.
reasons.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo supports the extension of UNSMIL's mandate and an inclusive, Libyan-led political process facilitated by the United Nations, in line with the position of the African Union and our previous voting record.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to advance the political process, enforce the arms embargo, and strengthen Libyan institutional integrity. In line with Council consensus and established practice, we vote in favour without making a statement prior to the vote.
reasons.France: France consistently supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate, the UN-facilitated political roadmap towards national elections, the preservation of the independence of sovereign economic institutions, and the withdrawal of all foreign forces and mercenaries.
reasons.Greece: Greece strongly supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to advance the Libyan-led political process, preserve institutional integrity, and ensure the full withdrawal of foreign forces and mercenaries in accordance with international law.
reasons.Latvia: Latvia fully supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to advance the Libyan-led political process, preserve institutional integrity, and ensure the withdrawal of all foreign forces and mercenaries. Given Council-wide consensus on the draft resolution, there is no need for an explanation of vote before the voting procedure.
reasons.Liberia: Liberia supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to foster Libyan-led political dialogue, preserve institutional stability, and promote national reconciliation in close partnership with the African Union.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan consistently supports the renewal of UNSMIL's mandate to assist the Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, preserve the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and facilitate credible national elections.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports UNSMIL's mandate and an inclusive, Libyan-led political process leading to national elections, as well as the preservation of Libya's sovereign institutions and assets. Given full Council consensus on the draft resolution, Panama votes in favour without delivering a statement prior to the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation consistently supports the extension of UNSMIL's mandate to facilitate a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political settlement and maintain international mediation efforts, with all key elements aligned with our position. Any remarks will be delivered after the adoption in line with standard practice.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNSMIL's mandate, which maintains crucial support for a Libyan-led political process, institutional reunification, and national reconciliation in close coordination with the African Union. In line with Council practice for consensual mandate renewals, Somalia reserves any national remarks for after the adoption.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: As the penholder and sponsor of the draft resolution, the United Kingdom fully supports renewing UNSMIL's mandate for another year and securing Council unity behind the UN-facilitated political process.
reasons.United States of America: The draft resolution aligns fully with United States policy by extending UNSMIL's mandate for 12 months, protecting Libya's financial and economic institutions, reinforcing the unified national budget, and calling for the departure of all foreign fighters and mercenaries.

before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
President,

As the penholder on Libya, the United Kingdom is pleased to put forward this draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for a further twelve months. 

At this critical juncture for Libya, the presence and active facilitation of UNSMIL remain indispensable. The resolution before us reaffirms the Security Council’s united support for an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, with the clear objective of delivering free, fair, transparent, and inclusive national elections to end the prolonged transition and unify the country's state institutions.

The text also underscores the essential need to preserve the integrity and independence of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya and the Audit Bureau, and condemns any attempts to use intimidation or force against them. It calls for sustained progress on the security track, full implementation of the ceasefire agreement, and the withdrawal of all foreign forces, fighters, and mercenaries.

We would like to thank all Council members for their constructive engagement throughout negotiations, which reflects our shared commitment to peace, stability, and prosperity for the Libyan people. The United Kingdom will vote in favour of the draft resolution and encourages all members to do the same.

Thank you.

after.Bahrain:
Mr. President,

The Kingdom of Bahrain welcomed the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for a period of twelve months, and we thank the United Kingdom, the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating this consensus.

Bahrain’s vote in favour of the resolution reaffirms our steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of brotherly Libya, as well as our continued support for the Libyan people in fulfilling their aspirations for security, stability, development, and prosperity.

My delegation reiterates that a lasting solution to the crisis can only be achieved through a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, that culminates in the holding of free, fair, transparent, and inclusive presidential and parliamentary elections. We urge all Libyan political stakeholders to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise to overcome outstanding differences, refrain from unilateral actions that deepen institutional divisions, and prioritize the supreme national interest of their country.

In this context, Bahrain stresses the critical importance of preserving the ceasefire agreement of 23 October 2020 and calls for the full implementation of the Action Plan approved by the 5+5 Joint Military Commission, including the synchronized, phased, and complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries without delay, and ending all forms of external interference in Libya’s internal affairs.

Furthermore, we emphasize the vital necessity of safeguarding the independence, integrity, and unified operation of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau. Libya's natural wealth belongs to all Libyans and must be managed equitably and transparently for their collective benefit.

In conclusion, the Kingdom of Bahrain commends the tireless efforts of UNSMIL and highlights the crucial supporting roles played by regional partners, particularly the League of Arab States and the African Union, in advancing national reconciliation. We reaffirm our full solidarity with brotherly Libya as it works towards enduring peace and institutional reunification.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL). We appreciate the efforts of the penholder, the United Kingdom, in consultations on the text.

The current political and security situation in Libya remains complex and fragile. Advancing the political transition and achieving long-term peace and stability is the shared aspiration of the Libyan people and the common expectation of the international community. China hopes that UNSMIL will continue to uphold the principle of a "Libyan-led and Libyan-owned" political process, strictly implement its mandate, maintain impartiality and objectivity, and actively mediate to assist all Libyan parties in bridging differences through dialogue and consultation, with a view to holding inclusive national elections at an early date and ending the prolonged transitional period.

Safeguarding national unity and institutional integrity is crucial for Libya’s recovery. China calls on all parties in Libya to exercise restraint, refrain from unilateral actions, and maintain the independence and unity of key sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Audit Bureau. Libya's natural resource revenues belong to all its people and should be managed transparently, equitably, and effectively for the benefit of the country’s development.

At the same time, the Security Council's original intention in freezing the assets of the Libyan Investment Authority was to protect the national wealth of the Libyan people, not to harm their interests. Relevant Member States and financial institutions should fully implement the relevant resolutions of the Security Council, including resolution 2819 (2026), protect the frozen assets, and facilitate their reasonable preservation and reinvestment to ensure that the legitimate rights and interests of the Libyan people are effectively safeguarded.

Peace and stability in Libya cannot be achieved without a secure and stable environment. China calls on all parties to strictly adhere to the ceasefire agreement, advance security sector reform, and achieve the withdrawal of foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries in a balanced and orderly manner. The international community should respect Libya's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity, and refrain from external interference. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue playing a constructive role in supporting the Libyan people to achieve lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

Thank you, President.
after.Colombia:
Mr. President,

Colombia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for a period of twelve months. We express our appreciation to the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its efforts in facilitating consensus around this text.

Colombia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. We firmly believe that sustainable peace can only be achieved through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, that culminates in the holding of free, fair, transparent, and credible national presidential and parliamentary elections. 

Our own national experience has shown that lasting stability requires genuine political dialogue, institutional reconciliation, and the constructive participation of all sectors of society. In this regard, we underscore the indispensable role of civil society and the full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation of women and youth in shaping Libya’s future.

We also stress the importance of preserving the integrity, transparency, and independence of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank and the National Oil Corporation. The resources of Libya belong to all the Libyan people and must be managed equitably and accountably, free from political pressure or armed intimidation.

Finally, Colombia reiterates its deep concern over the human rights situation, particularly the vulnerability of migrants, refugees, and internally displaced persons. We call upon all Libyan parties to fully respect their obligations under international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and to advance meaningful progress on security sector reform and the disarmament, demobilisation, and reintegration of armed groups.

Colombia reiterates its full support for UNSMIL and the Special Representative of the Secretary-General in their tireless efforts to accompany the Libyan people on their path towards lasting peace, democracy, and prosperity.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Democratic Republic of the Congo:
Monsieur le Président,

La République démocratique du Congo salue l’adoption unanime de la résolution renouvelant pour douze mois le mandat de la Mission d’appui des Nations Unies en Libye (MANUL). Notre vote favorable témoigne de notre soutien indéfectible au peuple libyen et à ses aspirations légitimes à la paix, à la stabilité, à la souveraineté et à l’intégrité territoriale de leur pays.

La présence et les bons offices de la MANUL demeurent essentiels pour accompagner un processus politique inclusif, inter-libyen et piloté par les Libyens eux-mêmes, sous l’égide des Nations Unies. À cet égard, nous réitérons notre appel à toutes les parties prenantes libyennes à surmonter leurs divergences, à préserver l’intégrité et l’indépendance des institutions souveraines et financières du pays, et à s’engager de bonne foi en vue de parvenir à un consensus permettant la tenue rapide d'élections présidentielle et législatives libres, transparentes et crédibles, afin de clore définitivement la période de transition.

Par ailleurs, ma délégation souligne l'importance primordiale de la mise en œuvre intégrale de l'accord de cessez-le-feu du 23 octobre 2020. Cela implique nécessairement le retrait complet, synchronisé et sans délai de l'ensemble des forces étrangères, des combattants étrangers et des mercenaires, dont la présence continue de menacer non seulement la sécurité de la Libye, mais également la stabilité de la région du Sahel et de l'ensemble du continent africain.

Enfin, la République démocratique du Congo tient à réaffirmer le rôle crucial de l'Union africaine et de son Comité de haut niveau sur la Libye dans les efforts de réconciliation nationale, et appelle à une coopération étroite et continue entre les Nations Unies, l'Union africaine et les organisations régionales pour appuyer la Libye sur la voie d'une paix juste et durable.

Je vous remercie.
after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which extends the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for a period of one year, until 31 October 2027. We thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its efforts and for guiding these negotiations toward a balanced and consensus-driven text.

By renewing UNSMIL’s mandate today, the Security Council sends an unequivocal message of unity and continued commitment to the Libyan people. Libya cannot remain trapped in a prolonged transitional phase, which only fuels institutional fragmentation, economic instability, and security risks. 

Our priority remains clear: to support a credible, inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, that leads without delay to free, fair, transparent, and inclusive presidential and parliamentary elections throughout the country. We urge all Libyan leaders and institutional actors to set aside narrow interests, engage in good faith in dialogue facilitated by UNSMIL, and reach the necessary political compromises to establish unified institutions and a viable electoral framework.

In this context, France stresses that Libyan actors must refrain from any unilateral decisions or use of force that could inflame tensions or undermine trust. We reiterate the vital necessity of preserving the independence, neutrality, and integrity of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau. The recent attempts to interfere with or use armed force against these institutions are unacceptable. Libya’s resources belong to all Libyans and must be managed equitably, transparently, and with proper accountability, underpinned by a unified national budget.

On the security track, preserving the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement remains paramount. France commends the work of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and encourages further steps toward the reunification of the security and military apparatus. The full implementation of the ceasefire agreement requires the synchronized and complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries from Libyan soil without further delay. We also recall the obligation of all States to respect and strictly enforce the United Nations arms embargo. In this regard, the European Union’s Operation IRINI continues to play a vital and impartial role in monitoring compliance on the high seas.

Finally, a lasting peace cannot be built without respect for international humanitarian law and human rights. We call for the protection of civic space, the meaningful participation of women and youth in the political process, and urgent measures to address the plight of migrants and refugees, including an end to arbitrary detention and accountability for violations.

France reaffirms its steadfast support for UNSMIL and will continue to work closely with the United Nations, its Council partners, and the Libyan people to achieve a stable, unified, and sovereign Libya.
after.Greece:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Greece welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for a period of twelve months, and we thank the penholder, the United Kingdom, for its constructive leadership throughout the negotiations.

As an immediate maritime neighbour, Greece attaches the utmost importance to the stability, sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. Today’s unanimous vote demonstrates the Council’s continued and resolute commitment to supporting the Libyan people in overcoming the prolonged transition and achieving enduring peace.

Greece reiterates its steadfast support for UNSMIL and its leadership. We firmly believe that a sustainable resolution to the Libyan crisis can only be achieved through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations. In this regard, we urge all Libyan political leaders and stakeholders to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise to resolve all outstanding contentious issues and swiftly agree on the viable constitutional and legal frameworks necessary to hold free, fair, transparent, and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections across the country.

Progress on the political track must be accompanied by tangible advancements on the security and economic tracks. The full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement remains critical. In this context, Greece underscores the urgent necessity of the complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries from Libyan territory without further delay, in line with relevant Security Council resolutions and the Action Plan of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission. 

Furthermore, full compliance with the United Nations arms embargo is essential to de-escalate tensions, prevent the illicit flow of weapons, and create an environment conducive to lasting stability. We also stress the importance of preserving the integrity, independence, and unified functioning of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions—including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau. Libya’s national resources must be managed transparently, equitably, and accountably, strictly for the benefit and prosperity of all Libyans, free from political pressure, intimidation, or unilateral action.

Mr. President,

Greece remains fully committed to standing by the Libyan people and supporting all multilateral efforts aimed at building a unified, stable, democratic, and prosperous Libya, fully integrated into its regional neighbourhood and respectful of international law.

I thank you.
after.Latvia:
President,

Latvia welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for another twelve months. We thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its dedicated efforts in facilitating consensus on this text.

The united voice of the Security Council today sends a clear signal of our steadfast support for UNSMIL, Acting Special Representative Stephanie Koury, and the Libyan people in their pursuit of lasting peace, stability, and democratic governance.

A sustainable solution to the prolonged crisis can only be achieved through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations. We urge all Libyan leaders and institutional actors to engage constructively, without preconditions and in a spirit of compromise, to overcome the persistent political deadlock and reach the necessary consensus to hold free, fair, transparent, and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections as soon as possible. Unilateral actions that entrench divisions and undermine trust must cease immediately.

Latvia remains deeply concerned by the fragile security situation, the continued proliferation of weapons, and the presence of foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries. Full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement and the synchronized, gradual withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries without delay remain essential for Libya’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as for broader regional stability.

We also underscore the critical importance of safeguarding the independence, neutrality, and integrity of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya and the Libyan Audit Bureau. Recent attempts to use intimidation or armed force against oversight bodies are unacceptable. Libya’s vast resources belong to all its citizens and must be managed equitably, transparently, and with strict accountability.

Finally, Latvia reiterates the paramount importance of upholding international human rights law and international humanitarian law. We call on Libyan authorities to protect civic space, ensure a safe environment for civil society and human rights defenders, guarantee the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women and youth, and address the grave situation faced by vulnerable migrants and refugees, including by ending arbitrary detention.

Latvia reaffirms its full commitment to supporting UNSMIL’s mandate and the aspirations of the Libyan people for a unified, sovereign, and prosperous future.

Thank you.
after.Liberia:
Mr. President,

Liberia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for an additional year.

Our vote reflects Liberia’s steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya, as well as our continued confidence in the vital role played by UNSMIL in facilitating an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process.

The prolonged transitional period continues to challenge Libya’s stability and the aspirations of its people. We reiterate our call to all Libyan political actors and stakeholders to rise above narrow interests, refrain from unilateral steps that heighten political tensions, and engage in genuine dialogue to resolve outstanding differences. The ultimate goal must remain the holding of free, fair, credible, and inclusive presidential and parliamentary elections as soon as possible.

Liberia welcomes the emphasis placed in the resolution on safeguarding the independence, integrity, and unified management of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya and the National Oil Corporation. Libya’s abundant natural resources belong to all its citizens and must be managed transparently, equitably, and with full accountability.

On the security front, we remain deeply concerned by recurring clashes, the illicit flow of weapons, and the presence of foreign fighters. We call for the full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement and the expedited, synchronized withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries. Comprehensive security sector reform and the reunification of national military and security institutions are essential for lasting peace.

We also underscore the critical role of regional partners, particularly the African Union and its High-Level Committee on Libya, in advancing national reconciliation and complementary peace efforts. Furthermore, Liberia emphasizes the paramount importance of upholding international human rights law and international humanitarian law, ensuring the protection of civilians, human rights defenders, and vulnerable groups, notably migrants and refugees.

In conclusion, Mr. President, Liberia reaffirms its full support to UNSMIL and looks forward to working constructively with all Council members and international partners to help the Libyan people realize their legitimate aspirations for peace, democracy, and sustainable development.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by the United Kingdom extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for another year.

Our position of principle remains unchanged: we consider UNSMIL to be a key instrument in assisting the Libyan parties to overcome the protracted political crisis that has gripped the country since the illegal foreign military intervention in 2011. The mission’s presence on the ground remains an important stabilizing factor.

We reiterate that any sustainable political settlement in Libya must be strictly Libyan-led and Libyan-owned, facilitated by the United Nations, and free from external interference, artificial deadlines, or imposed solutions from abroad. The primary objective remains the holding of free, fair, and inclusive national presidential and parliamentary elections, which are vital for ending the prolonged transitional period, overcoming institutional division, and restoring the national unity and sovereignty of Libya.

To achieve this, it is essential that the Mission maintain an objective, balanced, and unbiased approach, engaging constructively with all major Libyan political forces and regional actors across the West, East, and South. In this regard, we continue to stress the importance of expanding UNSMIL’s presence across the entirety of Libya’s territory, including through the active functioning of its offices in Benghazi and Sabha.

We also attach great importance to safeguarding the independence, integrity, and unified operation of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Audit Bureau. Libya's natural resources and revenues belong to all Libyans and must not be used as leverage in political rivalries or subjected to unilateral interference.

On the security track, we continue to support the work of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission towards the reunification of the military and security institutions. At the same time, we reaffirm that any withdrawal of foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries must be conducted in a synchronized, phased, gradual, and balanced manner, so as not to disrupt the fragile balance of power on the ground or undermine the 2020 ceasefire.

We hope that the renewed mandate will enable UNSMIL to focus its efforts effectively on facilitating a comprehensive political dialogue and assisting the Libyan people in achieving long-awaited peace, stability, and prosperity.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council (A3), namely the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Liberia, and my own country, Somalia.

At the outset, the A3 expresses its sincere appreciation to the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its dedicated efforts in guiding the consultations that led to the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for another twelve months. The unity demonstrated by the Council today sends a clear and reassuring message of our collective commitment to supporting the Libyan people on their path towards lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

The A3 reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. We firmly believe that sustainable peace can only be achieved through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations. In this regard, we urge all Libyan political stakeholders to engage constructively with UNSMIL and with one another, in a spirit of compromise, to resolve outstanding contentious issues and finalize the necessary constitutional and legal frameworks to hold free, fair, transparent, and credible national presidential and parliamentary elections as soon as possible, thereby bringing an end to the prolonged transitional period.

We also stress the vital importance of national reconciliation as the bedrock of enduring peace. The A3 underscores the critical role played by regional organizations, particularly the African Union and its High-Level Committee on Libya, in advancing the national reconciliation process, and we encourage continued coordination between the United Nations, the African Union, and the League of Arab States.

Mr. President,

The preservation of the integrity, independence, and unified functioning of Libya’s sovereign economic and financial institutions—including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau—is essential for the country’s stability. We condemn any attempts to exert political pressure, use force, or deploy armed intimidation against these institutions. Libya’s natural wealth belongs to all Libyans and must be managed transparently, equitably, and accountably. Furthermore, the A3 reiterates that Libya’s frozen assets must be protected and preserved to safeguard their value for the future benefit of the Libyan people, in line with relevant Council resolutions.

On the security front, we remain concerned by sporadic tensions and clashes between armed groups. We call for the full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the coordinated and complete withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries without delay, in accordance with the Action Plan of the 5+5 Joint Military Commission. We also emphasize the urgency of advancing comprehensive security sector reform and disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration (DDR) processes.

In conclusion, the A3 reiterates its full support for UNSMIL and its leadership. We stand in complete solidarity with the Libyan people in their pursuit of peace, stability, and unified democratic governance.

I thank you.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) for another twelve months. We thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its diligent work in guiding this Council to a united outcome.

Today’s unanimous vote sends an unmistakable message of Council support for UNSMIL, its leadership, and the Libyan people. A capable and fully empowered UN mission remains indispensable to facilitating an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process aimed at ending the protracted transitional period and delivering free, fair, transparent, and credible national presidential and parliamentary elections. 

Recent developments remind us of the fragility of Libya’s institutions and the risks of political deadlock. The United States reiterates its call on all Libyan actors to refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions or risk reigniting conflict. We strongly condemn any attempts to use force, intimidation, or political interference against sovereign economic and oversight institutions, including the Central Bank of Libya, the National Oil Corporation, and the Libyan Audit Bureau. Safeguarding the independence and integrity of these institutions is essential for the country's stability.

Libya’s vast natural resources belong to all Libyans and must never be politicized or used as leverage for partisan gain. As reaffirmed in this resolution, energy revenues must be managed in a transparent, equitable, and accountable manner, including by ensuring that payments for crude oil exports are routed exclusively through the accounts of the National Oil Corporation at the Libyan Foreign Bank. We continue to urge full implementation and adherence to a unified national budget to ensure macroeconomic stability and provide vital services for the Libyan people.

Finally, durable peace will not be possible without progress on the security track. The United States calls for the full implementation of the October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the urgent withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters, and mercenaries from Libyan territory without further delay. We also reiterate the necessity of upholding the UN arms embargo and advancing security sector reform and disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration.

The United States remains steadfast in its partnership with the Libyan people and will continue to work closely with UNSMIL and our international partners to support Libya on its path toward lasting unity, sovereignty, and prosperity.

Thank you, Mr. President.
